arxiv-1912-01470.title: Structural and electronic properties of the pure and stable elemental 3D topological Dirac semimetal α \alpha -Sn
arxiv-1912-01470.creator: Ivan Madarevic, Umamahesh Thupakula, Gertjan Lippertz, Niels Claessens, Pin-Cheng Lin, Harsh Bana, Sara Gonzalez, Giovanni Di Santo, Luca Petaccia, Maya Narayanan Nair, Lino M.C. Pereira, Chris Van Haesendonck, Margriet J. Van Bael
arxiv-1912-01470.description: Abstract In-plane compressively strained α \alpha -Sn films have been theoretically predicted and experimentally proven to possess non-trivial electronic states of a 3D topological Dirac semimetal. The robustness of these states typically strongly depends on purity, homogeneity and stability of the grown material itself.

arxiv-2101-05109.title: Bose-Hubbard models with on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions: Exactly solvable case
arxiv-2101-05109.creator: Saidakhmat Lakaev, Shokhrukh Kholmatov, Shakhobiddin Khamidov
arxiv-2101-05109.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Saidakhmat Lakaev, Shokhrukh Kholmatov, Shakhobiddin Khamidov. We study the discrete spectrum of the two-particle Schrödinger operator H ^ μ ​ λ ​ ( K ) , \widehat{H}_{\mu\lambda}(K), K ∈ 𝕋 2 , K\in\mathbb{T}^{2}, associated to the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian ℍ ^ μ ​ λ \widehat{\mathbb{H}}_{\mu\lambda} of a system of two identical bosons interacting on site and nearest-neighbor sites in the two dimensional lattice ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}^{2} with interaction magnitudes μ ∈ ℝ \mu\in\mathbb{R} and λ ∈ ℝ , \lambda\in\mathbb{R}, respectively.

arxiv-2107-13184.title: Numerical wave propagation aided by deep learning
arxiv-2107-13184.creator: Hieu Nguyen, and, Richard Tsai
arxiv-2107-13184.description: Abstract We propose a deep learning approach for wave propagation in media with multiscale wave speed, using a second-order linear wave equation model. We use neural networks to enhance the accuracy of a given inaccurate coarse solver, which under-resolves a class of multiscale wave media and wave fields of interest.

arxiv-2209-13417.title: On general-relativistic Lagrangian perturbation theory and its non-perturbative generalization
arxiv-2209-13417.creator: Thomas Buchert *, Ismael Delgado Gaspar, Jan J. Ostrowski
arxiv-2209-13417.description: Abstract The Newtonian Lagrangian perturbation theory is a widely used framework to study structure formation in cosmology in the nonlinear regime. We review a general-relativistic formulation of such a perturbation approach, emphasizing results on already developed extensive formalism including among other aspects: the non-perturbative modeling of Ricci and Weyl curvatures, gravitational waves and pressure-supported fluids.

arxiv-2303-08292.title: Box-Constrained L 1 / L 2 L_{1}/L_{2} Minimization in Single-View Tomographic Reconstruction
arxiv-2303-08292.creator: Sean Breckling, Malena I. Español, Victoria Uribe, Chrisitan Bobmara, Jordan Pillow, Brandon Baldonado
arxiv-2303-08292.description: Abstract We present a note on the implementation and efficacy of a box-constrained L 1 / L 2 L_{1}/L_{2} regularization in numerical optimization approaches to performing tomographic reconstruction from a single projection view. The constrained L 1 / L 2 L_{1}/L_{2} minimization problem is constructed and solved using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM).

arxiv-2311-18803.title: BioCLIP : A Vision Foundation Model for the Tree of Life
arxiv-2311-18803.creator: Samuel Stevens, Jiaman Wu, Matthew J Thompson, Elizabeth G Campolongo, Chan Hee Song, David Edward Carlyn, Li Dong, Wasila M Dahdul, Charles Stewart, Tanya Berger-Wolf, Wei-Lun Chao, Yu Su
arxiv-2311-18803.description: Abstract Images of the natural world, collected by a variety of cameras, from drones to individual phones, are increasingly abundant sources of biological information. There is an explosion of computational methods and tools, particularly computer vision, for extracting biologically relevant information from images for science and conservation.

arxiv-2312-04470.title: GaitGuard: Towards Private Gait in Mixed Reality
arxiv-2312-04470.creator: Diana Romero, Ruchi Jagdish Patel, Athina Markopoulou, Salma Elmalaki
arxiv-2312-04470.description: Abstract Augmented/Mixed Reality (AR/MR) technologies usher in a new era of immersive, collective experiences, differentiating them from traditional mobile systems. As these technologies evolve, prioritizing privacy and security is critical. This paper focuses on gait privacy, where gait — the way a person walks — can reveal sensitive information such as age, ethnicity, or disorders.

arxiv-2312-06942.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
arxiv-2312-06942.creator: Ryan Greenblatt ∗ Buck Shlegeris Kshitij Sachan Fabien Roger Redwood Research
arxiv-2312-06942.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) become more powerful and are deployed more autonomously, it will be increasingly important to prevent them from causing harmful outcomes. Researchers have investigated a variety of safety techniques for this purpose, e.g. using models to review the outputs of other models, or red-teaming techniques to surface subtle failure modes.

arxiv-2401-09276.title: Wafer-scale fabrication of mesoporous silicon functionalized with electrically conductive polymers
arxiv-2401-09276.creator: Manfred May, Mathis Boderius, Natalia Gostkowska-Lekner, Mark Busch, Klaus Habicht, Tommy Hofmann, Patrick Huber
arxiv-2401-09276.description: Abstract The fabrication of hybrid materials consisting of nanoporous hosts with conductive polymers is a challenging task, since the extreme spatial confinement often conflicts with the stringent physico-chemical requirements for polymerization of organic constituents. Here, several low-threshold and scalable synthesis routes for such hybrids are presented.

arxiv-2405-01517.title: New Tools for Smoothed Analysis: Least Singular Value Bounds for Random Matrices with Dependent Entries
arxiv-2405-01517.creator: Aditya Bhaskara, Eric Evert, Vaidehi Srinivas, Aravindan Vijayaraghavan
arxiv-2405-01517.description: Abstract We develop new techniques for proving lower bounds on the least singular value of random matrices with limited randomness. The matrices we consider have entries that are given by polynomials of a few underlying base random variables. This setting captures a core technical challenge for obtaining smoothed analysis guarantees in many algorithmic settings.

arxiv-2406-02753.title: Toward improved property prediction of 2D materials using many-body quantum Monte Carlo methods
arxiv-2406-02753.creator: Daniel Wines, Jeonghwan Ahn, Anouar Benali, Paul R. C. Kent, Jaron T. Krogel, Yongkyung Kwon, Lubos Mitas, Fernando A. Reboredo, Brenda Rubenstein, Kayahan Saritas, Hyeondeok Shin, Ivan Štich, Can Ataca
arxiv-2406-02753.description: Abstract The field of 2D materials has grown dramatically in the past two decades. 2D materials can be utilized for a variety of next-generation optoelectronic, spintronic, clean energy, and quantum computing applications. These 2D structures, which are often exfoliated from layered van der Waals materials, possess highly inhomogeneous electron densities and can possess short- and long-range electron correlations.

arxiv-2411-09998.title: Adaptive Non-uniform Timestep Sampling for Accelerating Diffusion Model Training
arxiv-2411-09998.creator: Myunsoo Kim, Donghyeon Ki, Seong-Woong Shim, Byung-Jun Lee
arxiv-2411-09998.description: Abstract As a highly expressive generative model, diffusion models have demonstrated exceptional success across various domains, including image generation, natural language processing, and combinatorial optimization. However, as data distributions grow more complex, training these models to convergence becomes increasingly computationally intensive.

arxiv-2503-00845.title: Rewarding Graph Reasoning Process makes LLMs more Generalized Reasoners
arxiv-2503-00845.creator: Miao Peng, Nuo Chen, Zongrui Suo, Jia Li
arxiv-2503-00845.description: Abstract . Despite significant advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs), developing advanced reasoning capabilities in LLMs remains a key challenge. Process Reward Models (PRMs) have demonstrated exceptional promise in enhancing reasoning by providing step-wise feedback, particularly in the context of mathematical reasoning.

arxiv-2511-11198.title: Geospatial Chain of Thought Reasoning for Enhanced Visual Question Answering on Satellite Imagery
arxiv-2511-11198.creator: Shambhavi Shanker, Manikandan Padmanaban, Jagabondhu Hazra
arxiv-2511-11198.description: Abstract Geospatial chain of thought (CoT) reasoning is essential for advancing Visual Question Answering (VQA) on satellite imagery, particularly in climate related applications such as disaster monitoring, infrastructure risk assessment, urban resilience planning, and policy support. Existing VQA models enable scalable interpretation of remote sensing data but often lack the structured reasoning required for complex geospatial queries.

pmc-10538090.title: The Fast and One-Step Growth of ZnO Nanorods on Cellulose Nanofibers for Highly Sensitive Photosensors
pmc-10538090.creator: Naveed ul Hassan Alvi, Mohammad Yusuf Mulla, Tiffany Abitbol, Andreas Fall, Valerio Beni, Antonios Kelarakis
pmc-10538090.description: Cellulose is the most abundant organic material on our planet which has a key role in our daily life (e.g., paper, packaging). In recent years, the need for replacing fossil-based materials has expanded the application of cellulose and cellulose derivatives including into electronics and sensing.

pmc-10617232.title: Engineering liquid metal-based nanozyme for enhancing microwave dynamic therapy in breast cancer PDX model
pmc-10617232.creator: Qiong Wu, Yongnian Yu, Xiaorui Yu, Qijun Du, Li Gou, Longfei Tan, Changhui Fu, Xiangling Ren, Jun Ren, Kai Xiao, Xianwei Meng
pmc-10617232.description: BackgroundsThe novel concept of microwave dynamic therapy (MDT) solves the problem of incomplete tumor eradication caused by non-selective heating and uneven temperature distribution of microwave thermal therapy (MWTT) in clinic, but the poor delivery of microwave sensitizer and the obstacle of tumor hypoxic microenvironment limit the effectiveness of MDT.

pmc-11447160.title: Differences in Mu rhythm when seeing grasping/motor actions in a real context versus on screens
pmc-11447160.creator: Celia Andreu-Sánchez, Miguel Ángel Martín-Pascual, Agnès Gruart, José María Delgado-García
pmc-11447160.description: Mu rhythm (∼8–12 Hz) in the somatosensory cortex has traditionally been linked with doing and seeing motor activities. Here, we aimed to learn how the medium (physical or screened) in which motor actions are seen could impact on that specific brain rhythm.

pmc-11478621.title: A Structural Equation Modelling Approach to Examine the Mediating Effect of Stress on Diet in Culturally Diverse Women of Childbearing Age
pmc-11478621.creator: Karim Khaled, Fotini Tsofliou, Vanora A. Hundley
pmc-11478621.description: Background: Stress has been shown to be associated with poor nutrition among young women. However, studies around the topic have major limitations in their methodologies and the role of confounding factors within this association remains unclear in the literature. Objective: To investigate the associations between stress and dietary quality/patterns in a culturally diverse population of childbearing-aged women.

pmc-11595740.title: Pulmonary Endometriosis: A Systematic Review
pmc-11595740.creator: Konstantinos Nikolettos, Alexandros Patsouras, Sonia Kotanidou, Nikolaos Garmpis, Iason Psilopatis, Anna Garmpi, Eleni I. Effraimidou, Angelos Daniilidis, Dimitrios Dimitroulis, Nikos Nikolettos, Panagiotis Tsikouras, Angeliki Gerede, Dimitrios Papoutsas, Emmanuel Kontomanolis, Christos Damaskos
pmc-11595740.description: Background/Objectives: Endometriosis is characterized by the presence of ectopic endometrial-like glands and stroma outside the endometrial cavity, which mainly occurs in the pelvic cavity. Pulmonary endometriosis, or thoracic endometriosis syndrome (TES), describes the rare presence of endometrial-like cells in the thoracic cavity and includes catamenial pneumothorax, catamenial hemothorax, hemoptysis, and lung nodules.

pmc-11736367.title: Curcumin enhances developmental competence and ameliorates heat stress in in vitro buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) embryos

pmc-12540095.title: Comparative effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual agonists in the treatment of patients with metabolic dysfunction associated steatohepatitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12540095.creator: Meng Li, Jianli Hu, Yip Han Chin, Han Shi Jocelyn Chew, Wenru Wang
pmc-12540095.description: BackgroundGlucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and dual agonists have been shown to induce histological improvements in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). However, current clinical evidence on their effectiveness in improving hepatic fibrosis and cardiovascular outcomes remains limited and inconsistent.MethodsThis study synthesized randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from major databases up to August 30, 2025, focusing on patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH.

pmc-12560691.title: Microvascular Decompression in a Patient With Positional Hemifacial Spasm: Case Report
pmc-12560691.creator: Christopher Adams, Ali Samii, Turner Peckham, Manuel Ferreira
pmc-12560691.description: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE:Hemifacial spasm (HFS) is known to be caused by certain activities and, in rare cases, has been shown to be position-dependent. This is the first case of HFS caused in a patient when lying in a prone position that completely resolved after surgical decompression.CLINICAL PRESENTATION:A 29-year-old female presented with HFS when lying in the prone position.

pmc-13052065.title: Optimizing Obesity Management With GLP‐1 Agonist Medication Through Mobile Health Technology, Nutrition Therapy, and Progressive Strength Training: A Retrospective Program Review
pmc-13052065.creator: Elizabeth Sharp Edens, Heather Falise, Rebecca Smith, Elle Bernardo
pmc-13052065.description: BackgroundGLP‐1 RAs are effective in treating obesity; however, they typically result in significant loss of skeletal muscle mass. Real‐world evidence to inform systematic guidelines and clinical implementation for preserving skeletal muscle mass and reducing cardiometabolic risk with lifestyle modifications on GLP‐1 RAs remains limited.

pmc-13188397.title: A machine learning approach to using ultrasound for body composition and nutritional status assessment in newborns: a pilot study protocol
pmc-13188397.creator: Bryan J. Ranger, Marisa Albert, Ji In Kim, Hayoung Cho, Julie Hohenberg, Keshi He, Donglai Wei, Melkamu Berhane, Tsinuel Girma, Judy Estroff, Katherine A. Bell, Jinhee Park
pmc-13188397.description: BackgroundAccurate assessment of infant body composition, specifically fat and fat-free mass, is crucial for evaluating growth and nutritional status. Existing methods, such as air displacement plethysmography and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, are expensive, require specialized facilities, and demand trained personnel. Ultrasound offers a promising alternative as a portable, low-cost tool capable of distinguishing adipose tissue from skeletal muscle.

pmc-13315685.title: Interim assessment by circulating tumor DNA in primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma: a multicenter LYSA study
pmc-13315685.creator: Vincent Camus, Daphné Krzisch, Alessio Bruscaggin, Emilie Lévêque, Mathieu Viennot, Luc-Matthieu Fornecker, Morgane Cheminant, Sébastien Bailly, Franck Morschhauser, Pierre Feugier, Sylvain Choquet, Eric Durot, Sylvain Carras, Caroline Delette, Gandhi-Laurent Damaj, Agathe Waultier-Rascalou, Pierre
pmc-13315685.description: Key Points•Genetic markers suitable for ctDNA-based MRD tracking were detectable in 98% of patients with PMBL.•Combined PET negativity and undetectable MRD after 4 cycles of immunochemotherapy identifies patients with excellent prognosis. Introduction Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (PMBL) is a rare, highly curable, aggressive subtype of large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL).

pmc-13482789.title: YES Oklahoma: Building Pathways into Cancer Research and Public Health for Indigenous High School Students
pmc-13482789.creator: Cara Monroe, Amy Lyons-Ketchum, Horvey Palacios, Justin Lund, John R. Walkup, Kent Smith, Stefan Wilhelm, Rajagopal Ramesh
pmc-13482789.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Youth Enjoy Science (YES) Oklahoma (OK) Scholars is an eight-week summer program that engages American Indian high school students in cancer and biomedical research. YES OK uses a relational, place-informed educational model, with a curriculum that emphasizes (1) increasing cancer biology and public health knowledge, (2) developing laboratory and scientific communication skills, (3) strengthening college and career preparation, and (4) connecting scientific learning to cultural and community contexts.

pmc-13556505.title: 308. The U-shaped relationships between prolactin level and insulin resistance in patients with schizophrenia under olanzapine treatment
pmc-13556505.creator: M-L Lu, K K Goh
pmc-13556505.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPatients with schizophrenia are at elevated risk for metabolic disturbances, particularly when treated with second-generation antipsychotics such as olanzapine. Prolactin elevation is a common adverse effect of antipsychotic therapy, yet its role in glucose homeostasis remains unclear.Aims & ObjectivesThis present study aimed to investigate the association between serum prolactin levels and insulin resistance among patients with schizophrenia receiving long-term olanzapine monotherapy.
